question: How is the second noble statement said with these many words to Hamsa and Hayagriva?
premises: The second noble statement uses this many words
Hamsa and Hayagriva are addressed as lord
The addressed one is Sadashiva yet called jiva
inference: The second statement identifies the addressed Hamsa Hayagriva as Sadashiva though named jiva.
uncertainties: etāvadbhiḥ may count words or syllables
haṃsa and hayagrīva may be separate deities or one compound address
plain_english: By these many words this second noble statement is made: O Hamsa, O Hayagriva, O lord, you are Sadashiva, supreme, though called the jiva.
